title: Are LLM-Generated Formal Specifications Faithful to Their Requirements? A Study on Bimodal Formal Specification Generation
abstract: arXiv:2610.32053v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Formal specification generation is a critical step towards formal verification and correctness assurance of software. Recently, large language models have been widely adopted in automatic generation of formal specifications. However, existing LLM-based specification generation approaches often assume that the input program is correct, which deviates from the real purpose of formal verification---to figure out whether the program meets its requirements when its correctness is unknown. Therefore, we conduct an empirical study of LLM-based specification generation under the bimodal setting: given both the natural language requirement and its corresponding code implementation, whose correctness is unknown. We construct a benchmark of 1,403 C programs and evaluate ACSL specification generation with Frama-C verification. translated_title: LLM生成的形式化规范是否忠实于其需求？一项关于双模态形式化规范生成的研究
translated_abstract: 形式化规范生成是实现软件形式化验证与正确性保证的关键步骤。近年来，大语言模型已被广泛应用于形式化规范的自动生成。然而，现有基于LLM的规范生成方法通常假设输入的程序是正确的，这偏离了形式化验证的真正目的——在程序正确性未知的情况下判断程序是否满足其需求。因此，我们在双模态设置下对基于LLM的规范生成开展了一项实证研究：同时给定自然语言需求及其对应的代码实现，且其正确性未知。我们构建了一个包含1,403个C程序的基准数据集，并结合Frama-C验证来评估ACSL规范的生成。我们的研究得出了若干有趣的发现：首先，当代码实现正确时，提供自然语言需求……
tldr: 本文针对程序正确性未知这一形式化验证的真实场景，开展了双模态（自然语言需求+代码实现）下LLM生成ACSL形式化规范是否忠实于需求的实证研究，构建了包含1,403个C程序的基准并用Frama-C进行验证评估。
en_tdlr: This paper presents an empirical study on whether LLM-generated formal specifications are faithful to their requirements in a bimodal setting where code correctness is unknown, constructing a benchmark of 1,403 C programs and evaluating ACSL specification generation with Frama-C verification.
